prose_slots: Short-time spectral estimation forms auto- and cross-spectra from recent records of the reference $u(t)$ and measured actuator displacement $y(t)$. To keep the spectral estimates responsive to evolving outer controller loop dynamics as the specimen degrades, each update uses a short recent record. These spectra support the subsequent identification of the outer controller loop response and estimation of the margin in {eq:bncf}. This subsection defines the windowed transforms, recursive averaging, and frequency bins used to form them.

The spectra are updated every $\Delta t=0.125\,\mathrm{s}$ using the most recent $T_w=0.5\,\mathrm{s}$ of both signals, so consecutive windows overlap by 75%. At $f_s=2048\,\mathrm{Hz}$, each window contains $N=f_sT_w=1024$ samples and has a Fourier-bin spacing of 2 Hz. where $w[r]=\tfrac{1}{2}\{1-\cos[2\pi r/(N-1)]\}$ is the Hann window and $\omega_m=2\pi mf_s/N$ is the angular frequency at bin $m$. The transforms give the instantaneous auto- and cross-spectra

The spectra are left unnormalized because normalization cancels in the ratios used below. The frequency argument $\omega_m$ is omitted for brevity. To reduce variation between windows, the instantaneous spectra are averaged recursively with exponential weighting [4], following the modified-periodogram approach of [3]. review: The opening identifies the spectra as quantities computed from recent u and y records. It now explains that short windows limit the time span represented while the outer controller loop dynamics change as the specimen degrades, without asserting that the spectra accurately track arbitrary rapid changes. The prose proceeds from window settings through transforms, instantaneous spectra, recursive averaging, and retained bins. The grammatical where continuation, supplied parameters and definitions, [3] and [4] attributions, and unknown-stiffness qualification are retained. The spectral averaging weight $\eta_s$ is identified without assigning an unsupported value. No displayed equation was changed.
